sections.title: Global asymptotic stability of homogeneous polynomial vector fields is undecidable
sections.abstract: For rational homogeneous polynomial vector fields, the authors reduce stability questions to cubic fields and prove global asymptotic stability is undecidable in every odd degree at sufficiently large fixed dimension.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove GAS is many-one complete for every odd degree ≥3 and all dimensions above a fixed threshold, hence cubic GAS is undecidable in some fixed dimension.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Rational-coefficient homogeneous polynomial vector fields on real Euclidean space; the dimension threshold is sufficiently large, not arbitrary.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper says its fixed dimension threshold is not computed; it does not identify the smallest dimension where undecidability begins.

sections.title: Anomalous scaling limit of a Brownian particle in a log-correlated potential
sections.abstract: At weak disorder, the authors establish a scaling limit for a diffusion in a log-correlated Gaussian potential, with a singular path law and Gaussian-multiplicative-chaos reversible measure; in dimension two they compute the scaling exponent exactly.
sections.claimed_result: Under the paper’s assumptions and sufficiently weak disorder, the authors prove convergence to a continuous strong Markov process with singular reversible measure and anomalous scaling.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Dimension d≥2; the random environment satisfies the paper’s stationarity, dependence, symmetry, and regularity hypotheses, with disorder below a dimension-dependent threshold.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is for weak disorder and this structured class of random fields; it does not establish the same behavior at strong disorder or for every log-correlated potential.

sections.title: Subspace Uncertainty and Sharp Sampling Thresholds on the Boolean Cube
sections.abstract: For Gaussian regression on a known subspace of low-degree functions on the Boolean cube, the paper gives an exponential worst-case sample threshold and sharpens an uncertainty bound, with an Airy-kernel construction showing the k^(1/3) remainder is generally unavoidable.
sections.claimed_result: For fixed q₀<1/2 and 1≤k≤q₀d, the worst-subspace sample threshold is (m+t) exp{d Ψ(k/d)+O(k^(1/3))}; the paper also proves a matching lower bound in specified regimes.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Squared population L₂ loss, Gaussian regression, known m-dimensional subspace of degree-at-most-k functions on the d-dimensional Boolean cube; the lower bound requires m≤binom(d, floor(k^(1/3))) or t≥m.
sections.unique_caveat: The matching lower bound is not asserted for every feasible m,t; the theorem’s stated asymptotic regime and confidence conditions matter.

sections.title: Directed fractal percolation and non-Lipschitz variants
sections.abstract: In Mandelbrot fractal percolation, the authors quantify last-passage growth and construct directed paths through open sites when paths may move exponentially fast in space, defining an unrectifiable directed-percolation variant.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show high last-passage values are obstructed for Lipschitz paths, while allowing exponentially fast spatial motion yields directed paths through open sites.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Mandelbrot’s scale-by-scale fractal percolation; not a theorem for general random media or Liouville quantum gravity.
sections.unique_caveat: The proposed non-Lipschitz variant changes the path constraint; it does not overturn the known absence of ordinary directed percolation in the basic model.

sections.title: The sharp L²-Michael–Simon inequality
sections.abstract: For isometric immersions of n-manifolds into Euclidean space with n≥3, the authors prove the sharp Michael–Simon Sobolev constant, characterize equality, and extend the argument to conformal ambient settings.
sections.claimed_result: For n≥3, the coefficient is the Aubin–Talenti constant n(n−2) Vol(Sⁿ)^(2/n)/4, independent of codimension; the authors characterize equality cases.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: An isometric immersion j:(Σⁿ,g)→Rᴺ and test functions in W^{1,2}(Σ); the paper takes manifolds to be connected.
sections.unique_caveat: The sharp theorem is stated for n≥3; equality has a specific conformal/capacity condition and is not simply a claim that every immersion attains equality.

sections.title: The moduli space of curves of genus 16 is uniruled
sections.abstract: Using non-abelian Brill–Noether theory, the authors claim that the moduli space of curves of genus 16 is uniruled, the highest genus for which they say this is known.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove M₁₆ is uniruled.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The statement concerns the moduli space of curves of genus 16; the abstract does not give further technical hypotheses.
sections.unique_caveat: The record claim and proof details come from a new preprint; its short abstract alone does not expose the construction or establish independent expert validation.

sections.title: Ordinary G-permutable subgroups of finite simple groups
sections.abstract: The paper classifies nontrivial proper ordinary G-permutable subgroups of finite non-abelian simple groups and claims to solve part (a) of Problem 17.112 in the Kourovka Notebook.
sections.claimed_result: Such subgroups occur exactly for the listed families PSL₂(q), ²B₂(2^(2a+1)), J₁, Sp₄(4), and PSp₄(p) with the stated congruence restrictions; the paper also classifies them.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite non-abelian simple groups; ordinary G-permutability and proper, nontrivial subgroups are the specific notion and scope.
sections.unique_caveat: This is not a classification of every broader notion of permutability or of subgroups in arbitrary finite groups.

sections.title: Prevalence of sparsity for negatively curved metrics
sections.abstract: On a closed manifold of any dimension, the authors prove that negatively curved Cᵏ metrics with exponentially sparse length spectra form a prevalent, hence dense, family for sufficiently large k.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish exponential sparsity of distinct closed-geodesic lengths for a prevalent set of negatively curved metrics, with an exponent growing sublinearly in regularity k.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Closed manifolds of arbitrary dimension and negatively curved Cᵏ metrics, for sufficiently large k.
sections.unique_caveat: Prevalence and density do not mean every negatively curved metric has this property; the theorem requires sufficiently high regularity.
